It differs from standard color rendering by accumulating vector-valued data via alpha-blending rather than scalar RGB values, allowing real-time vision-language tasks [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the method differs from standard color rendering by 'accumulating vector-valued data via alpha-blending rather than scalar RGB values'. The evidence supports the part about accumulating vector-valued data (feature vectors) via alpha-blending (Equation 15 in S2). However, the evidence does not support the claim that this is done 'rather than scalar RGB values' in the context of the entire rendering process. Standard 3D Gaussian Splatting renders both color (scalar RGB) and features (vector) simultaneously using the same alpha-blending mechanism. The evidence describes adding feature vectors *to* the Gaussians, not replacing the scalar RGB rendering entirely. Furthermore, the claim implies a fundamental difference in the accumulation mechanism itself ('rather than'), whereas the evidence shows it is an extension (adding features) to the existing framework. Therefore, only part of the claim is supported.
